message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell** (often referred to as a *multinucleated giant cell*). In some contexts—especially during development or in certain tissues—a group of fused cells forms a larger cell-like structure known as a **syncytium**, which also contains multiple nuclei within a shared cytoplasm.
